quarterly_data.quarter: American Electric Power press release: AEP Advances Innovative Energy Solution for Google with (10-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Customer Google: AEP plans to invest approximately $4 billion to advance a new 702-megawatt fuel cell generation project near Cheyenne, Wyoming, under a long-term 20-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with Google. Under the PPA, Google will acquire power from Cheyenne Fuel Cell, LLC. AEP and its partners plan to start construction in 2026, and the facility is expected to be fully operational by the end of 2028. The planned facility uses fuel cell technology developed by Bloom Energy that generates electricity without combustion of natural gas, and the project includes plans to integrate carbon capture technology; it follows agreements reached between Google and Black Hills Corp., effective Sept. 30. CEO Bill Fehrman: the project 'demonstrates how we are creating new opportunities to meet evolving energy needs for customers both within and beyond our traditional service territory.'
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $4 billion investment; 702 MW; 20-year PPA; construction start 2026; fully operational by the end of 2028
